sections.html:
Dubois County is in southwest Indiana, and Jasper is the county seat and largest city. The 2020 census counted 43,637 people in the county and 16,703 in Jasper. Manufacturing is the largest employment sector, with furniture and cabinet makers well known in Jasper, followed by retail and health care.

Whatever the employer, anyone selling a house here needs a clear tax record before closing.

sections.h2: The Assessor's office and yearly dates
sections.html:
The Dubois County Assessor is at One Courthouse Square, Jasper, IN 47546. The phone number is 812-481-7010, the email is assessor@duboiscountyin.org, and hours are Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

These dates repeat each year:

  • January 1: the assessment date
  • April 1: Form 136 property tax exemption applications are due
  • May 15: business personal property returns are due, moving to the next business day if it falls on a weekend
  • December 31: affidavits for destroyed or removed property are due

The office also requires a Notice of Assessment Registration when a project needs no building permit, with a $100 civil penalty for failure to file. If you built or removed a structure, tell the assessor before a buyer's review.

You appeal a Dubois County assessment with Form 130, which the assessor's site links under "Appeal an assessment." The deadline is June 15 of the year the notice or tax bill is mailed.

One petition covers one parcel. After the assessor's informal meeting, the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals holds a hearing within 180 days of filing, with notice mailed at least 30 days ahead. A $50 penalty may apply if you miss the hearing with no valid continuance. Disputes go on to the Indiana Board of Tax Review through Form 131.

The Dubois County tax sale usually happens in September or October for parcels with a balance due from the spring of the prior year or earlier. In mid-July, the Auditor's office usually mails a certified letter to each listed owner.

Dubois County tax sale steps
StepWhat happens
Added costA $130.00 tax sale charge is added to each parcel's amount due
PublicationNames are published in local newspapers if taxes remain unpaid
SaleOnline or live at the County Courthouse
Minimum bidTotal owed on the parcel through the current year
PaymentHigh bidder pays the Treasurer the same day, in cash or certified funds
RedemptionThe owner has one year, then the Auditor issues a deed to the certificate holder

Owners can pay up to the time of the sale. Contact the Treasurer at One Courthouse Square, Jasper, at 812-481-7080 or treasurer@duboiscountyin.org, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Indiana sets two installment dates, May 10 and November 10, and the date moves to the next business day when it lands on a weekend.

The late penalty is 5% if you pay within 30 days of the due date and have no earlier delinquency, and 10% otherwise. Later installments can bring extra 10% penalties.

The standard homestead deduction has been 60% of assessed value up to $48,000, filed by January 5, and the rule was amended effective January 1, 2025. Confirm the current figure with the Assessor.

Sellers in Dubois County commonly deal with inherited homes, outdated houses and unpaid tax. Before closing, Indiana requires a sales disclosure form that the assessor reviews before the deed reaches the auditor, one form per parcel.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the current balance and any tax sale charges.
  • Check the assessor's records for additions or removed structures.
  • Collect estate documents and prior tax bills.
  • Decide whether to repair or sell as is.

A cash purchase can close quickly, with taxes settled at the title company from your proceeds.

Timing can save money. A parcel with a balance from the spring of the prior year or earlier can land on the tax sale list, and the $130.00 charge is added once it is listed. If you are near that point, pay or sell before the July letter goes out. Pay attention to the mid-July certified letter and the September or October sale, since owners can pay up to the moment of the sale.

When you gather papers for a closing, include the latest tax bill, any estate documents, and a note of any building you added or tore down. The assessor's record should match what a buyer will see on the lot, so a missing registration or an old structure still on the card can be cleared up before the sales disclosure form goes in.

faqs.q: Where is the Dubois County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: At One Courthouse Square, Jasper, IN 47546. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and the phone is 812-481-7010.

faqs.q: When does the Dubois County tax sale happen?
faqs.a: Usually in September or October. A certified letter normally goes to listed owners in mid-July, and owners can pay up to the time of the sale.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem Dubois County property after a tax sale?
faqs.a: The prior owner has one year to redeem the tax certificate. After that the Auditor's office gives a deed to the certificate holder.

faqs.q: What is the Dubois County tax sale charge?
faqs.a: A $130.00 charge is added to each parcel's amount due once it is listed for tax sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dubois County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance and penalties are paid from your proceeds at closing, and selling before the sale date avoids the added tax sale charge.
